title: Overlap down the bond axis
statement:
Which overlap can generate a sigma bond?

[_]{a}

choices: Two p orbitals aligned end-on along the axis
Parallel p orbitals overlapping side by side
A lone pair already localized on a distant atom
Any two orbitals merely because they have the same n
explanations: Their lobes point along the bond direction.
There is no appreciable overlap in this setup.

hints: Sigma symmetry has electron density along the internuclear axis for a bonding orbital.
Point the orbitals toward one another.
solution: Sigma symmetry has electron density along the internuclear axis for a bonding orbital. Point the orbitals toward one another. End-on overlap produces sigma symmetry. Their lobes point along the bond direction.
